questions.question: Who founded the value of ‘G’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'__Henry Cavendish__'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __**Key points**__

 
• The **gravitational constant** (also known as the **universal gravitational constant**, the **Newtonian constant of gravitation**, or the **Cavendish gravitational constant**), denoted by the capital letter *G*, is an empirical physical constant involved in the calculation of gravitational effects in Sir Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation and in Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity.
 
• In Newton's law, it is the** proportionality constant** connecting the** gravitational force between two bodies with the product of their masses and the inverse square of their distance**.
 
• The Einstein field equations, it quantifies the relation between the** geometry of spacetime and the energy–momentum tensor** (also referred to as the stress–energy tensor).
 
• The measured value of the constant is known with some certainty t**o four significant digits.**
 
• In SI units, its value is approximately **6.674×10−¹¹ m³⋅kg−¹⋅s−²**
 
• The modern notation of Newton's law involving *G* was introduced in the 1890s by C. V. Boys.
 
• The first implicit measurement with an **accuracy within about 1%** is attributed to** Henry Cavendish in a 1798 experiment.**

questions.question: Who introduced the concept of virtual water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Anthony Allan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Anthony Allan** introduced the concept of virtual water.
 
• Virtual water refers to the hidden flow of water if food or other commodities are traded from one place to another.
 
• This concept helps in understanding the amount of water used in the production and trade of goods.
 
• It is a crucial concept for water-scarce regions and for global water management strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Anthony Allan** was awarded the Stockholm Water Prize in 2008 for his contribution to the concept of virtual water.
 
• The concept of virtual water has significant implications for understanding water use in agricultural and industrial processes.
 
• By considering virtual water, countries can make better decisions regarding water resource management and trade policies.

questions.question: When did Michael Faraday discover electromagnetic induction, the principle behind the electric transformer and generator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1831**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in the year **1831**.
 
• This discovery is crucial as it laid the foundation for the development of **electric transformers and generators**.
 
• Faraday's experiment involved moving a magnet through a coil, which generated an electric current within the coil, demonstrating the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• His work on electromagnetic induction is considered one of the most significant contributions to the field of electromagnetism and electrical engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**

 
 
• It is the production of voltage or electromotive force due to a change in the magnetic field.
 
• This phenomenon is the principle behind transformers, inductors, and many types of electrical generators.
 
 
 
• **Michael Faraday**
 
 
• He was an English scientist who contributed significantly to the study of electromagnetism and electrochemistry.
 
• Faraday's laws of electrolysis and his work on the Faraday effect are also notable contributions.
 
 
 
• **Electric Generators**
 
 
• Devices that convert mechanical energy into electrical energy using the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• Generators are widely used in power plants to produce electricity for homes and industries.
 
 
 
• **Transformers**
 
 
• Electrical devices that transfer electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction.
 
• They are used to increase (step-up) or decrease (step-down) voltage levels in power transmission and distribution systems.

questions.question:
Natural language processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that helps computers ______ human language.

I. understand

II. Interpret

III. manipulate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Natural Language Processing (NLP) **is a **subfield of artificial intelligence and computational linguistics. **
 
• It focuses on the interaction between computers and humans through natural language.
 
• **Understanding**: NLP enables computers to comprehend human language as it is spoken or written.
 
 
• This involves understanding the semantics, syntax, and context of the language.
 
 
 
• **Interpretation: **NLP also involves the interpretation of human language by computers.
 
 
• This refers to the process of parsing the input, determining its meaning, and potentially transforming it into another format or language.
 
 
 
• **Manipulation**: Furthermore, NLP allows for the manipulation of human language.
 
 
• This could involve tasks like text generation, translation, summarization, and more.
 
• The combination of understanding, interpretation, and manipulation allows for a wide range of applications.
 
• These include chatbots, sentiment analysis, machine translation, voice recognition, and many more.
 
 
 
• ***Therefore, all three options (I, II, III) are correct. NLP involves the understanding, interpretation, and manipulation of human language by computers.***
 
• The development and refinement of NLP technologies are continually evolving, making human-computer interactions more natural, intuitive, and effective.
 
• Overall, the goal of NLP is to make computers as proficient as possible at understanding and responding to** human language, allowing for more natural and intuitive human-computer interaction.**

questions.question: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier** is widely regarded as the **father of modern chemistry**.
 
• He was instrumental in the chemical revolution of the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature.
 
• Lavoisier's work laid the foundation for the **law of conservation of mass**, which states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• He also helped develop the modern system for naming chemical substances, which replaced the older, less systematic names.
 
• His contributions significantly advanced the field of chemistry and helped transition it from alchemy to a more empirical and systematic science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joseph Priestley** also **discovered oxygen** independently around the same time as Lavoisier, but did not recognize it as an element.
 
• **Dame Kathleen Lonsdale** was a renowned **crystallographer**, not directly related to the chemical revolution.
 
• **Svante August Arrhenius** was a Swedish scientist known for his **theory of electrolytic dissociation** and contributions to physical chemistry, but he was active in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

questions.question: What are the two major file systems in Microsoft Windows?
questions.solution:
• There are two major file systems in Microsoft Windows, namely, **NTFS and FAT.**
 
• **FAT (File Allocation Table) **is generally supported by the Microsoft Windows OS and the system was inherited from old DOS.
 
• Whereas, **NTFS** is a file system that supports larger file sizes and hard drives. **NTFS is the default file system of the Windows NT family.**

questions.question: Who among the following confirmed Maxwell's theories with the discovery of radio waves and also became the first person to transmit and receive controlled radio waves in 1886?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heinrich Hertz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heinrich Hertz**

 
 
• Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell, who developed a unified theory of electromagnetism in the 1870s, predicted the existence of radio waves.
 
• Later, Heinrich Hertz, a German physicist, applied Maxwell's theories to the production and reception of radio waves.
 
• Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi after several years starting in 1894 built the first complete, commercially successful wireless telegraphy system based on airborne Hertzian waves or the radio waves in the year 1895.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Hopkinson’s test:__

 
 
• It is a full load test, used to test the efficiency of a DC machine.
 
• Temperature rise and commutation can be observed and maintained in the limit because this test is done under full load condition.
 
• It requires two identical machines that are coupled to each other. One of these two machines is operated as a generator to supply the mechanical power to the motor and the other is operated as a motor to drive the generator.
 
• It is also called a regenerative test or back to back test or heat run test.
 
 
 
• Guglielmo Marconi
 
 
• Italian physicist and inventor of the successful wireless telegraph (1896).
 
• He received the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1909.
 
• He worked on the development of shortwave wireless communication, which constitutes the basis of nearly all modern long-distance radio.
 
• It meant a giant leap – from an era of communication using wires to communicating without using wires. (Wireless).
 
 

 
• Michael Faraday:

 
 
• He is known as the Father of Electricity.
 
• He discovered the laws of electromagnetism.
 
• He also discovered the induction of electric current.
 
• He also discovered benzene in the year 1825.
 
• He also built the first electric generator and first electric motor.

questions.question: Who among the following made the first the compound microscope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Zacharias Janssen.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A Dutch father-son team named **Hans **and **Zacharias Janssen** invented the first so-called compound microscope in the late **16th century** when they discovered that if they put a lens at the top and bottom of a tube and looked through it, objects on the other end became magnified.
 
• A compound microscope is a** high-power** (high magnification) microscope that uses a **compound lens system.**
 
• A compound microscope has** multiple lenses**: the **objective lens** is compounded (multiplied) by the **eyepiece lens **to obtain a high magnification.
 
• **Higher magnification** is achieved by using two lenses rather than just a single magnifying lens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of the compound microscope:**

 
 
• **Eyepiece**: ​Also known as the ocular, is the lens that you look through at the top of the microscope. Standard eyepieces typically have a **10x** magnification power.
 
• **Eyepiece Tube**: The eyepieces are held in place above the objective lens by the Eyepiece Tube. A** diopter adjustment ring **is frequently included in** binocular microscope** heads to account for probable irregularities in human eyesight in one or both eyes. A diopter is not required when using a **monocular (single eye)** microscope.
 
• **Objective Lenses:** These are the** primary optical lenses **on a microscope. 
 
• **Nosepiece:** It houses the objectives. The objectives are exposed and are mounted on a rotating turret so that different objectives can be conveniently selected.
 
• **Coarse and Fine Focus knobs**: These are used to **focus** the microscope.
 
• **Stage:** The specimen to be examined is put on the stage. When working at greater magnifications, when careful motions of the specimen slide are necessary, a mechanical stage is used.
 
• **Stage clips:** When there is no mechanical stage, stage clips are employed. To observe different areas of the specimen, the viewer must manually move the slide.
 
• **Aperture**: The opening in the stage through which the base (transmitted)** light **reaches the stage is known as an aperture.
 
• **Illuminator**: It is a** light source** for a microscope that is normally situated in the **microscope's base.** **Low-voltage halogen bulbs **with continuous variable illumination control are used in most light microscopes.
 
• **Condenser**: The light from the illuminator is collected and focused on the specimen by the condenser. It's usually found** beneath the stage,** along with an iris diaphragm.
 
• **Iris Diaphragm**: The **amount of light** that reaches the specimen is controlled by the Iris Diaphragm. It's beneath the stage and above the condenser. An** Abbe condenser** with an iris diaphragm is standard on most high-end microscopes.
 
• **Condenser Focus Knob**: It adjusts the **lighting focus **on the specimen by moving the condenser up or down.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7a441628094529c71f9849b3821282614bfa56f0e4e60f2974c955fc93b4057.png]

questions.question: In which of the following modes of data transmission, can the data flow in both directions but in only one direction at a time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Half Duplex__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The method of communication in which transmission can take place in both directions, but happens only in one direction at a time, is called half-duplex communication__.

 __
 
• In this mode of communication, data can be sent and received, but not at the same time.
 
• Instead, data is transmitted in one direction, then the communication channel switches to transmit data in the opposite direction.
 
• This mode of communication is commonly used in walkie-talkies, two-way radios, and some forms of computer networking.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Duplex communication is a method of communication in which data can be transmitted and received simultaneously in both directions.
 
• Simplex communication is a method of communication in which data can only be transmitted in one direction, from the sender to the receiver, and not in the opposite direction.
 
 
• In other words, in simplex communication, data can flow in only one direction along a communication channel.

questions.question: Researchers of Kerala-based Amrita University in collaboration with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority have developed a real-time _______. This system can help save lives and prevent loss to property by issuing advance alerts.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Researchers of **Kerala-based Amrita University** in collaboration with the **Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority **have developed a real-time **Landslide warning system****.**
 
• The system gives advance warnings of landslides so that people can be safely evacuated before disaster strikes.
 
• After successfully deploying India’s first such system in Kerala’s Western Ghats, it will now be deployed in Sikkim to guard against rainfall-induced landslides in the Sikkim-Darjeeling belt. 
 
• The system collects real-time, continuous data from the sensors, performs basic analysis at the Field Management Center (FMC) located on the site in Sikkim and relays it to the Data Management Center (DMC) at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham in Kerala’s Kollam district.
 
• The project is jointly funded by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, Government of India, and **Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham**.
 
• **Extra:-__**
 
• In 2008, Amrita set up **India's first landslide laboratory** which can create small landslides under controlled conditions and act as the feedback system for field deployment.
 
• **Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham **has been ranked 8th among the Indian universities by NIRF in 2019.

questions.question: In 1887, whose experiment was an attempt to find the velocity of the Earth with respect to the hypothetical luminiferous ether?

• **Albert Michelson and Edward Morley** conducted the **Michelson–Morley experiment** in **1887** with the aim of measuring the **Earth's velocity relative to the luminiferous ether**.

• The luminiferous ether was a theoretical concept hypothesized as the medium through which light waves propagate.
 
• In the 19th century, it was widely believed that just as water waves require a medium to travel through, light waves also required such a medium.

• **Pieter Zeeman, **a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz for discovering the Zeeman effect, which describes the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
 
• **Hendrik Antoon Lorentz,** also a Dutch physicist, shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman for their joint discovery and theoretical explanation of the Zeeman effect, and made significant contributions to the theory of electromagnetism and the electron theory of matter.

questions.question: What numerical scale was introduced in 1932 that determined the electronegativity of fluorine to be 4.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pauling scale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity,** a concept pioneered by **Linus Pauling in 1932,** measures an atom's ability within a molecule to attract electrons towards itself. It's described as "the power of an atom in a molecule to attract electrons to itself."
 
• On the Pauling scale, fluorine is set as the benchmark with an electronegativity of 3.98, and other elements are gauged relative to this value.
 
• Essentially, an atom's electronegativity indicates its tendency to pull electron density towards itself when forming bonds.
 
• Higher electronegativity signifies a stronger pull on electrons during bonding.
 
• Atomic number and atomic radius largely influence an atom's electronegativity.
 
• Across the periodic table, electronegativity generally increases from left to right and from bottom to top.
 
• Consequently, fluorine stands as the most electronegative element, while francium exhibits the least electronegativity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Allred-Rochow Electronegativity **method quantifies the electrostatic force resulting from the effective nuclear charge acting on the valence electrons of an atom.
 
• Mulliken's scale of electronegativity defines electronegativity as an inherent characteristic of an element, solely contingent on the valence state of the atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity** is the measure of an atom's ability to attract shared electrons in a covalent bond. A higher electronegativity value indicates a stronger attraction for the shared electrons. 
 
• This property follows a predictable trend across the periodic table: electronegativity generally increases from bottom to top within groups and from left to right across periods. 
 
• Consequently, fluorine holds the title of the most electronegative element, whereas francium ranks among the least electronegative.

• **Prussian blue tablets** - provides 100 per cent absorption from the gut and other portals of entry to the human body and are highly effective in incorporating Radio Cesium (Cs-137) and Radio Thallium.
 
• Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) injection - traps uranium in the guts and blood of victims during a nuclear accident or warfare.
 
• Ca-EDTA Respiratory Fluid - inhalation formula for chelation, or grabbing, of heavy metals and radioactive elements deposited in lungs through inhalation at nuclear accident sites. When injected into the veins, it “grabs” heavy metals and minerals and removes them from the body.
 
• Anti-gamma ray skin ointment - protects and heals the radiation damage on the skin.
 
• Amifostine injection - conventional radiopharmaceutical that limits damage from gamma radiation.
 
• Radioactive urine/biofluid collector - can safely dispose of the urine of a person affected by radiation.

questions.question: ______ based farming system is developed to improve environmental control over production of fish.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "__**Biofloc**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Biofloc technology** was developed in the **1990s** as a way for **fish** and **shrimp** farmers to **conserve** **feed** **inputs** and **utilize** **wastewater** during **production**.
 
• The main concept is that producers could piggyback off the** nitrogen cycle** and let beneficial bacterial colonies proliferate in culture water.
 
• To achieve Biofloc, producers needed to maintain a higher carbon to nitrogen ratio in their ponds.
 
• This would stimulate the growth of heterogeneous bacteria – microbes that break down organic carbon from the surrounding environment.
 
• The **bacterial growth (flocs)** could consume nitrogenous **fish wastes** and **toxic** **metabolites** before being eaten by the cultured species.
 
• This would reduce both the **environmental** **footprint** of **production** and **feed costs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bottom**-**dwelling** species like **shrimp** and **tilapia** are best suited to **biofloc production.**
 
• Since the bacterial load in the water is constantly shifting, fish must be relatively resistant to environmental challenges.
 
• **Sensitive** **species** will **not** **thrive** in this environment.

questions.question: When did Carl Friedrich Gauss and Wilhelm Eduard Weber invent the world's first electromagnetic telegraph?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1833.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carl Friedrich Gauss** and **Wilhelm Eduard Weber** invented the **world's first electromagnetic telegraph** in **1833.**
 
• The telegraph was capable of** transmitting signals **over long distances using **electricity and magnetism.**
 
• Gauss and Weber's invention paved the way for **modern communication systems,** including the internet.
 
• Gauss was a **renowned mathematician and physicist**, known for his contributions to **number theory, astronomy, and geodesy.**
 
• Weber was a** physicist **who worked closely with Gauss and made significant contributions to the** study of electricity and magnetism.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** electromagnetic force** that exists between **electrically charged particles **is the subject of the branch of physics known as **electromagnetism.**
 
• One of the four **fundamental forces**, the electromagnetic force, manifests electromagnetic fields like** magnetic fields, electric fields, and light. **
 
• In interactions between atoms and molecules, it is the **dominant force.**

questions.question: As per physicists and their major contributions/discoveries, Which of the following pair is INCORRECT?

options.text: Louis Victor de Broglie - Wavenature of matter

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paul Dirac - Liquid helium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paul Dirac's **major contribution was the development of **quantum electrodynamics**, which explains the interaction between** light and matter.**
 
• He** did not** work on **Liquid helium.**
 
• **John Bardeen, **along with his colleagues, developed the **theory of superconductivity**, for which he was awarded the** Nobel Prize in Physics twice**.
 
• **Louis Victor de Broglie **proposed the concept of **wave-particle duality**, which suggests that particles can exhibit **wave-like behavior.**
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1929** for his work on wave nature of matter.
 
• **Victor Francis Hess **discovered **cosmic rays,** which are **high-energy particles** that originate from outside the solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Bardeen** is also known for his work on the invention of the **transistor,** a device that revolutionized the field of electronics.
 
• **Louis Victor de Broglie's** work on **wave-particle duality** was a key contribution to the development of** quantum mechanics.**
 
• **Victor Francis Hess's **discovery of **cosmic rays** helped to advance our understanding of the** universe and its origins.**
 
• **Paul Dirac **was known for his contributions to the development of **quantum mechanics** and his prediction of the **existence of antimatter.**
